articles.title: TouchTree: I Built a Website That Tells You to Close It
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What if a website's entire purpose was to convince you to stop using websites? We spend so much time building te…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What I Built What if a website's entire purpose was to convince you to stop using websites? We spend so much time building technology to keep people engaged, scrolling, clicking, and coming back. I wanted to make something that did the opposite. Meet TouchTree — a tiny, interactive website that reminds you to step away from your screen and experience the world outside. It doesn't have a productivity dashboard, daily streaks, achievements, or notifications. It simply encourages you to feel the grass beneath your feet, touch the bark of a tree, smell a flower, listen to the wind, and be present for a moment. The experience has three simple stages: A reminder that the real world is waiting outside.
articles.author: Rohan Sonu Bablani

articles.title: TouchGrass AI: Less Scrolling, More Exploring with Open-Source AI
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass. 🌿 TouchGrass AI — Less Scrolling, More Exploring TouchGrass AI is a web application designed to encourage peop…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass . What I Built 🌿 TouchGrass AI — Less Scrolling, More Exploring TouchGrass AI is a web application designed to encourage people to spend less time on screens and more time exploring the natural world. The idea is simple: instead of using technology only for entertainment, we can use AI to inspire real-world experiences. Users can generate outdoor missions, explore nature-inspired activities, and earn points for completing challenges. Examples include observing different leaves, listening to birds, exploring trees, and taking mindful walks. The project is designed for students, nature lovers, and anyone who wants to develop healthier screen habits while discovering the world around them.

articles.title: Teste de Caixa Preta
articles.excerpt: Introdução Teste de caixa preta é o teste que avalia o software apenas pelo comportamento externo: você fornece entradas, observa as saídas e compara com o resultado esperado pela especificação. O tes…
articles.body: Introdução Teste de caixa preta é o teste que avalia o software apenas pelo comportamento externo : você fornece entradas, observa as saídas e compara com o resultado esperado pela especificação. O testador não olha o código-fonte, a estrutura interna nem a lógica de implementação. O que ele valida? Os testes se baseiam em requisitos, regras de negócio, casos de uso e user stories, e não no código. Por isso o teste vale para qualquer nível (unitário, integração, sistema, aceitação) e para testes funcionais e não funcionais.
articles.author: Yuri Peixinho

articles.title: Qwen-Image 2.1 on 16 GB of VRAM, quantized to NF4: a real benchmark against FLUX
articles.excerpt: On a 16 GB RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo does not fit in bf16 (the pipeline is 32.5 GB). Quantized to NF4 with bitsandbytes it does, and I ran it against the FLUX.1-dev Q6_K + pixel-art LoRA…
articles.body: On a 16 GB RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo does not fit in bf16 (the pipeline is 32.5 GB). Quantized to NF4 with bitsandbytes it does, and I ran it against the FLUX.1-dev Q6_K + pixel-art LoRA that made my blog covers: same prompts, same seeds, same card, every image checked by eye. What I measured Speed: 8.4 s per image for Qwen NF4 (8 steps) against 61 s for FLUX + LoRA (30 steps), median, 1344×768. About 7×. Text in the image: 13 of 18 requested texts exact for Qwen NF4, 7 for FLUX. Unquantized Qwen on a 48 GB A6000 got 17. Cover prompts: Qwen NF4 drew the requested scene in 11 of 15 covers; FLUX + LoRA in none (6 almost, 9 missing the main action or object). Memory: 11.9 GiB over the card's baseline for Qwen NF4 (nvidia-smi), 13.1 GiB for FLUX.
articles.author: Efrain Garay

articles.title: What Is Kerberoasting? How Can Attackers Crack Service Account Passwords Without Exploiting a Vulnerability?
articles.excerpt: An attacker with a regular domain account requests a service ticket. The domain controller issues it. No vulnerability was exploited. No alarm fires. And if the service account's password is weak enou…
articles.body: An attacker with a regular domain account requests a service ticket. The domain controller issues it. No vulnerability was exploited. No alarm fires. And if the service account's password is weak enough, the attacker may eventually recover it offline without ever making another authentication request. This is Kerberoasting: an attack that exploits the gap between how Kerberos was designed to work and how service accounts are often deployed and managed. The Kerberos Pieces Readers Actually Need Kerberos is a network authentication protocol designed to let parties prove their identities without sending passwords over the wire. Understanding Kerberoasting requires a working mental model of a few components.

articles.title: Visualizing a Mixed-Entity DynamoDB Table: What Schema Inference Reveals—and What It Misses
articles.excerpt: Introduction One of the most interesting aspects of Amazon DynamoDB is that a table does not need to represent a single business entity. In a relational database, we might create separate tables for u…
articles.body: Introduction One of the most interesting aspects of Amazon DynamoDB is that a table does not need to represent a single business entity. In a relational database, we might create separate tables for users, orders, and products, with foreign keys connecting related records. DynamoDB supports a different approach: multiple entity types can coexist in a single table, using carefully designed partition keys, sort keys, and secondary indexes to support application access patterns. This is commonly called single-table design . However, single-table design introduces an interesting challenge: how do we understand the logical structure of a table when the physical database does not enforce a complete schema for every item?

articles.title: NASA Demonstrates Next-Generation Heat Shield Technologies
articles.excerpt: NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24th cargo resupply missi…
articles.body: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) A KREPE-3 capsule floats inside the Northrup Grumman Cygnus XL 24 cargo spacecraft on October 7. Inside the capsule is a 3-D printed heat shield designed by researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. NASA NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24 th cargo resupply mission for NASA undocked from the International Space Station, it carried a fleet of 12 small, experimental capsules designed to test the next generation of thermal protection materials that could serve as the foundation for future heat shields.
